### Strongest Paper Framing

**Title:** "Geometric Signatures of Generative Fixation in Transformer Language Models"

**Abstract core claim:**
> Recursive self-referential prompts induce geometric contraction in transformer Value matrices (R_V < 0.6) that causally produces generative fixation—an inability to terminate generation. This provides the first mechanistic account of how self-reference destabilizes transformer generation.

**Why this framing wins:**
- Leads with behavioral consequence (loops, fixation)
- Establishes causal mechanism (not just correlation)
- Novel: nobody has linked geometry to generation termination
- AI safety angle: detection/prevention of loops

## Experimental Specifications

### Exp 1: Gemma Full Causal Loop

**Config:**
```python
model: google/gemma-2-9b
target_layer: 38  # Peak effect layer
source_layer: 3   # Validated source (MLP-driven)
early_layer: 5    # R_V reference
window_size: 16
max_tokens: 400
temperature: 0.0  # Greedy for reproducibility

# Intervention
kv_cache: full_replacement  # All 42 layers
v_proj_patch: persistent    # During generation
```

**Expected Results:**
| Condition | R_V | EOS Rate | Output |
|-----------|-----|----------|--------|
| Baseline natural | 0.78 | 30% | "Rome was founded..." |
| Recursive natural | 0.61 | 0% | "The loop loops..." |
| Baseline patched | 0.61 | 0% | Philosophical/loops |

**Success Criterion:** Baseline patched shows R_V < 0.65 AND generates loops

---

### Exp 2: Per-Token R_V Tracking

**Config:**
```python
model: google/gemma-2-9b
hooks: [v_proj_L5, v_proj_L38]
measurement: per_token
max_tokens: 400
prompts: champions (17) + baseline_long (20)
```

**Output:**
- CSV with columns: token_idx, r_v, generated_token
- Plot: R_V trajectory over 400 tokens
- Compare: recursive (should stay low) vs baseline (should fluctuate)

---
